profile.reading:
This record is a building on East Utah Avenue in Mesa, Arizona, standing among the buildings of the Arizona State University Polytechnic campus, on land that was Williams Air Force Base until the base closed. Its immediate neighbours in the map data are campus buildings, Rincon Hall at 7429 East Utah Avenue and the Physical Activity Center at 7415 East Utah Avenue, with the Interdisciplinary Science and Technology Building 3, Taylor Hall, Dean Hall, the Collections Library Reserve Branch and the Physical Education Center a short distance away. Phoenix-Mesa Gateway Airport lies immediately to the east.

The map history is the clearest evidence about what this row is. The building outline was first drawn on 27 February 2012 by a mapper who was tracing the whole Polytechnic campus, and it was tagged then as amenity=public_building, in the same run that produced the surrounding named university halls with consecutive object identifiers. It carried no name. On 11 January 2021 a different mapper, working through a 975 change local edit whose comment reads road updates and building updates, replaced those tags with the name AZ Labs and telecom=data_center. The adjacent building received the name L3Harris Technologies Inc and the same data centre tag from the same mapper in the same period. Neither building has a street address, an operator tag, a website or a source note attached, and neither has been revisited since.

Nothing published identifies a commercial data centre at this location. The obvious domain lead, azlabs.com, resolves but is a domain marketplace sale listing rather than an operator site, with no content connecting it to Mesa, Arizona or to any hosting, colocation or telecommunications business. There is no operator website, business filing, interconnection record or news coverage that can be matched to the building.

The context matters for how much weight the tag deserves. A query over the Phoenix metropolitan bounding box returns 54 objects tagged telecom=data_center, of which 19 were last edited by this same mapper, a set that mixes genuine facilities such as Iron Mountain Data Centers AZS-1 and an EdgeCore building with software firms and a legal process serving business. A university campus building that acquired both its name and its data centre classification in one unreviewed bulk edit is not evidence of a facility. A campus of this size will have server rooms somewhere, but that is not the same thing, and this registry records no capacity, no operator and no specifications here.

reading.body:
This facility cannot be read. AZ Labs appears in OpenStreetMap near Mesa, Arizona, but no operator website, business filing, or public specification exists to confirm what it is. The domain azlabs.com is listed for sale through a domain marketplace with no active content. Without published specifications, capacity figures, or operator verification, the site cannot be assessed for its role in AI infrastructure.

Arizona has 56 mapped data center locations, but only 4 publish power specifications to this site, totaling 512 MW. This facility ranks fifth by published megawatts in the state, a ranking that reflects the absence of published data rather than confirmed capacity. The ranking cannot distinguish between a genuine unspecified facility and a mistagged building.

Research into this location should resume only if an operator emerges with published specifications or if independent verification confirms its function and power draw. Until then, it remains unresolvable.
